614	- [ ] **Step 9: Rewrite `_async_tick_impl` to use state machine**
615	
616	Replace the full method (lines 472-630). The logic is the same but uses `self._state` instead of `self._dirty`, `self._in_sync`, and `self._tick_in_sync`:
617	
618	```python
619	    async def _async_tick_impl(self) -> None:
620	        """Core tick logic — called from _async_tick for LOADING and OUT_OF_SYNC states.
621	
622	        This is the single authoritative place for all sync state mutations:
623	        circuit breaker tracking, sync operations, and ``_last_set_pin``
624	        changes.
625	        """
626	        slot_state = self._resolve_slot_state()
627	        if slot_state is None:
628	            # State resolution failed — stay in current state and retry.
629	            return
630	
631	        expected_in_sync = self.calculate_in_sync(slot_state)
632	
633	        # -- LOADING: detect initial sync state without performing operations --
634	        if self._state is SyncState.LOADING:
635	            if slot_state.active_state not in (STATE_ON, STATE_OFF):
636	                if not self._logged_invalid_state:
637	                    _LOGGER.debug(
638	                        "%s: Active entity has invalid state '%s', waiting "
639	                        "for valid state (ON/OFF)",
640	                        self._log_prefix,
641	                        slot_state.active_state,
642	                    )
643	                    self._logged_invalid_state = True
644	                return
645	
646	            if expected_in_sync:
647	                self._state = SyncState.SYNCED
648	                if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON:
649	                    async_delete_issue(
650	                        self._hass,
651	                        DOMAIN,
652	                        f"slot_disabled_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
653	                    )
654	            else:
655	                self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
656	
657	            _LOGGER.debug(
658	                "%s: Initial state loaded, state=%s",
659	                self._log_prefix,
660	                self._state.value,
661	            )
662	            self._write_state()
663	            return
664	
665	        # -- OUT_OF_SYNC: check coordinator suspend flag, then attempt sync --
666	        if self._coordinator.suspended:
667	            self._state = SyncState.SUSPENDED
668	            self._write_state()
669	            return
670	
671	        if expected_in_sync:
672	            # Became in sync without us doing anything (external change)
673	            self._state = SyncState.SYNCED
674	            self._reset_sync_tracker()
675	            self._write_state()
676	            if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON:
677	                async_delete_issue(
678	                    self._hass,
679	                    DOMAIN,
680	                    f"slot_disabled_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
681	                )
682	                async_delete_issue(
683	                    self._hass,
684	                    DOMAIN,
685	                    f"slot_suspended_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._coordinator.lock.lock.entity_id}",
686	                )
687	            return
688	
689	        # Circuit breaker check (set operations only)
690	        if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON and self._sync_attempts_exceeded():
691	            _LOGGER.error(
692	                "%s: Sync attempts exceeded (%s in %s window), suspending lock",
693	                self._log_prefix,
694	                self._sync_attempt_count,
695	                SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW,
696	            )
697	            self._suspend_lock(
698	                f"Lock **{self._lock.lock.entity_id}**: slot "
699	                f"**{self._slot_num}** failed to sync after "
700	                f"{self._sync_attempt_count} consecutive attempts. "
701	                f"The lock may be rejecting the code silently or "
702	                f"experiencing communication issues. "
703	                f"Sync has been suspended for this lock. It will "
704	                f"resume automatically when the lock recovers.",
705	            )
706	            return
707	
708	        # Perform sync
709	        self._state = SyncState.SYNCING
710	        try:
711	            await self._perform_sync(slot_state)
712	        except CodeRejectedError as err:
713	            _LOGGER.error("%s: Code rejected: %s", self._log_prefix, err)
714	            await self._disable_slot(
715	                f"Lock **{err.lock_entity_id}**: slot **{err.code_slot}** "
716	                f"has been disabled. {err}\n\n"
717	                f"Fix the issue and re-enable the slot.",
718	            )
719	            # After disable, the slot active switch turns off. The next
720	            # _request_sync_check will see the slot as in-sync (no code
721	            # desired, no code on lock). Set to OUT_OF_SYNC so the next
722	            # tick resolves to SYNCED.
723	            self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
724	            return
725	        except (LockDisconnected, LockOperationFailed) as err:
726	            _LOGGER.info(
727	                "%s: Lock disconnected during %s usercode: %s. Will retry on next tick.",
728	                self._log_prefix,
729	                "set" if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON else "clear",
730	                err,
731	            )
732	            self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
733	            return
734	        except Exception as err:
735	            _LOGGER.exception(
736	                "%s: Unexpected error during %s usercode. "
737	                "Sync suspended for this lock to prevent infinite retry loop. "
738	                "Error: %s: %s",
739	                self._log_prefix,
740	                "set" if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON else "clear",
741	                type(err).__name__,
742	                err,
743	            )
744	            self._suspend_lock(
745	                f"Lock **{self._lock.lock.entity_id}**: slot **{self._slot_num}** "
746	                f"encountered an unexpected error during sync. This may indicate a bug "
747	                f"in the lock code manager integration. Check logs for details and "
748	                f"report this issue.\n\nError: {type(err).__name__}: {err}",
749	            )
750	            return
751	        else:
752	            # Sync succeeded — refresh coordinator to verify.
753	            # Skip for push providers — they update coordinator optimistically
754	            # via push_update() and refreshing from cache could read stale data.
755	            if not self._lock.supports_push:
756	                try:
757	                    await self._coordinator.async_refresh()
758	                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
759	                    _LOGGER.exception(
760	                        "%s: Coordinator refresh failed after sync operation. "
761	                        "Sync may have succeeded but verification failed. "
762	                        "Will retry on next tick.",
763	                        self._log_prefix,
764	                    )
765	                    self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
766	                    return
767	
768	        # Check if sync actually worked
769	        slot_state = self._resolve_slot_state()
770	        if slot_state is not None and self.calculate_in_sync(slot_state):
771	            self._state = SyncState.SYNCED
772	            self._reset_sync_tracker()
773	            self._write_state()
774	            if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON:
775	                async_delete_issue(
776	                    self._hass,
777	                    DOMAIN,
778	                    f"slot_disabled_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
779	                )
780	                async_delete_issue(
781	                    self._hass,
782	                    DOMAIN,
783	                    f"slot_suspended_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._coordinator.lock.lock.entity_id}",
784	                )
785	        else:
786	            self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
787	            self._write_state()
788	```

887	```python
888	    """Manage sync state for a single lock x slot combination.
889	
890	    Compares desired state (from entity states: active, PIN) against actual
891	    state (from coordinator data) and drives set/clear operations to reconcile.
892	
893	    Uses a state machine (SyncState) with five states: LOADING, SYNCED,
894	    OUT_OF_SYNC, SYNCING, SUSPENDED. State changes mark the slot for
895	    re-evaluation; reconciliation happens on the next tick. Includes circuit
896	    breaker protection that suspends the lock after repeated sync failures.
897	
898	    The in-sync binary sensor entity reads manager.in_sync and
899	    manager.sync_status for display.
900	
901	    State mutation rules:
902	        - ``_request_sync_check`` transitions SYNCED -> OUT_OF_SYNC or
903	          SUSPENDED -> OUT_OF_SYNC for immediate UI feedback.
904	        - ``_async_tick_impl`` is the single authoritative place for all
905	          other state transitions, circuit breaker, sync operations,
906	          and ``_last_set_pin`` changes.
907	
908	    Lifecycle methods (async_start, async_stop) are idempotent and re-entrant.
909	    """
910	```

## Result: NEAR-PASS with one gap

**GAP — Confidence: 85**

The LOADING → OUT_OF_SYNC transition has no dedicated test. `test_initial_state_is_loading` (line 399) checks that after a tick the state is *in* `{SYNCED, OUT_OF_SYNC}` but never explicitly tests the OUT_OF_SYNC outcome. `test_loading_to_synced` (line 414) only tests the SYNCED branch. The production path in `_async_tick_impl` lines 523-524 is exercised, but there is no test that sets up a mismatched slot from LOADING and asserts the final state is `SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC`.

To close this gap, a test like the following should be added to `TestSyncStateMachine`:

```python
async def test_loading_to_out_of_sync(
    self,
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
) -> None:
    """LOADING transitions to OUT_OF_SYNC when slot is not in sync on startup."""
    entity_obj = get_in_sync_entity_obj(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)
    manager = entity_obj._sync_manager
    manager._state = SyncState.LOADING
    # Make coordinator data mismatch (slot active but lock has empty code)
    manager._coordinator.data[1] = SlotCode.EMPTY
    await async_trigger_sync_tick(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY, set_dirty=False)
    assert manager._state is SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
```

All other spec requirements are fully met. The implementation is clean and consistent with the spec.

`_suspend_lock` is called with a `return` statement right after in the callers (lines 574-575, 613-619). That's correct.

Now let me verify the behavior when `_last_set_pin` is set in `_perform_sync` at line 329 (before `_record_sync_attempt`). If `_record_sync_attempt` throws (it doesn't, it's purely in-memory), but if the coordinator refresh fails after `_perform_sync`, `_last_set_pin` is still updated, which is correct because we did successfully issue the set.

Let me check whether there's a missing `_write_state()` in the final `else` case of the post-sync check. Specifically when `slot_state is None` after the successful sync:

Lines 638-656:
```python
slot_state = self._resolve_slot_state()
if slot_state is not None and self.calculate_in_sync(slot_state):
    ...SYNCED...
    self._write_state()
else:
    self._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC
    self._write_state()
```

The `else` branch at line 654-656 runs when `slot_state is None` OR `not calculate_in_sync(slot_state)`. Both cases correctly set `OUT_OF_SYNC` and call `_write_state()`. ✓

Now let me check the `_request_sync_check` missing `_write_state` issue: when state is `SYNCED` and `slot_state is None`, we stay SYNCED but no write state call is needed (state didn't change). ✓

Let me look at one more test concern — the `TestCalculateInSync` test uses `_manager()` as a `MagicMock(spec=SlotSyncManager)`. Let me verify the attribute binding works correctly:

At lines 51-54:
```python
mgr = MagicMock(spec=SlotSyncManager)
mgr._last_set_pin = last_set_pin
mgr.calculate_in_sync = SlotSyncManager.calculate_in_sync.__get__(mgr)
```

`SlotSyncManager.calculate_in_sync.__get__(mgr)` binds `calculate_in_sync` to the mock as if `mgr` were `self`. Since `calculate_in_sync` only uses `self._last_set_pin`, and that's set on the mock, this pattern is correct. ✓

Now let me check the issue with the "clear operation does not increment tracker" test — the test verifies this at the `_sync_attempt_count` level but doesn't actually run through the `_async_tick` path with a clear:

Looking at `test_clear_operation_does_not_increment_tracker` (line 1070): it calls `SERVICE_TURN_OFF` (disabling slot) then `_async_force_sync_cycle`. This doesn't explicitly trigger `_async_tick`. Let me check if the coordinator refresh triggers the tick:

`_async_force_sync_cycle` calls `coordinator.async_refresh()` and then fires time change. The time change fires `async_track_time_interval` callback, which calls `_async_tick`. So the tick IS invoked. The test correctly verifies counter stays at 0 after clear. ✓

Summary of findings:

**1. Minor convention violation**: `caplog.text` assertion in `test_sync.py` line 288.

**2. The race condition question**: `_request_sync_check` during `_async_tick_impl` is correctly handled — the `SYNCING` guard in `_request_sync_check` means it's a no-op while a sync is in progress. The HA event loop's single-threaded nature means callbacks can only fire at `await` points. No race condition.

**3. Missing edge case (`_resolve_slot_state` returns None in `_request_sync_check`)**: This is intentional and documented — the state stays `SYNCED`, and the next tick handles it. Not a bug.

**4. State machine transitions**: All transitions appear correct. The `_write_state()` calls are only needed when transitioning between states that produce different `in_sync` boolean values, and the code correctly omits redundant calls when transitioning between states that all map to `in_sync = False`.

## Result: Approved with one minor convention violation

The state machine logic is sound, the tests cover the right behaviors, and there are no bugs or meaningful race conditions. One convention violation found.

---

### Minor: caplog.text assertion in test_sync.py

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.claude/worktrees/sync-state-machine/tests/test_sync.py`, line 288

**Confidence:** 85

**Violation:** Project convention (from memory file `feedback_caplog_checks.md`) states: "Minimize caplog text assertions, prefer checking parameters or structured data."

```python
assert "Failed to disable slot" in caplog.text
```

This assertion checks a log message string to verify the exception was logged. The same behavioral guarantee is already structurally verified two lines later by checking the issue registry (`issue_registry.async_get_issue(...) is not None`). The caplog check is partially redundant and fragile — it would break on log message wording changes.

**Fix:** Either remove it (the issue registry assertion is sufficient to confirm the fallback path ran), or replace it with a log record check if confirming `_LOGGER.exception` was called is important:
```python
assert any(r.levelname == "ERROR" and "Failed to disable slot" in r.message for r in caplog.records)
```
Though removing it entirely is preferable per convention.

---

### Answers to the specific questions asked

**1. Bugs or logic errors in state machine transitions:** None found. All five states (LOADING, SYNCED, OUT_OF_SYNC, SYNCING, SUSPENDED) transition correctly. The `_write_state()` omissions on SYNCING → OUT_OF_SYNC transitions (lines 592, 601, 634) are intentional and correct — both states map to `in_sync = False` so no HA state update is needed.

**2. Race conditions with `_request_sync_check` during `_async_tick_impl`:** Not a real concern. `_request_sync_check` is a `@callback` (synchronous) and HA's event loop is single-threaded — it can only execute at `await` points. While `_async_tick_impl` is mid-execution with `self._state = SyncState.SYNCING`, `_request_sync_check` guards `if self._state is SyncState.SYNCED` and the `SYNCING` state is explicitly called out as a no-op in the docstring. No issue.

**3. Missing edge case — `_resolve_slot_state()` returns None during `_request_sync_check`:** Handled. Line 451: `if slot_state is not None and not self.calculate_in_sync(slot_state)` — if `None`, no transition occurs. The state stays SYNCED and the next tick re-evaluates. This is the documented design intent (request_sync_check is for UI feedback optimization, not authoritative reconciliation). Not a bug.

**4. Code style:** Matches existing conventions. No `nonlocal`/`global`, no Google-style docstrings, no inline imports. The for-loops in `_build_entity_id_map` and `_ensure_entities_ready` are not replaceable with comprehensions due to their mutation/early-return semantics respectively.

**5. Test quality:** Tests are well-structured and cover the right scenarios: initial state loading, all major state transitions, circuit breaker, error handling paths (CodeRejectedError, LockDisconnected, LockOperationFailed, unexpected exceptions), catch-all to targeted tracking upgrade, and the `calculate_in_sync` logic matrix. One convention violation noted above.

I have now reviewed all the changed files, the test suite, and the relevant source code. Here is my complete review.

---

## Code Review: Sync State Machine (Issue #1061)

### What was done well

The implementation is clean, well-structured, and achieves its stated goal. Specific strengths:

- The `SyncState` enum in `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.claude/worktrees/sync-state-machine/custom_components/lock_code_manager/models.py` is well-documented with clear state descriptions.
- The state machine eliminates three loosely-coupled boolean flags (`_dirty`, `_in_sync`, `_tick_in_sync`) with a single authoritative `_state` field -- a significant improvement in reasoning about sync behavior.
- The `suspended` flag on the coordinator at `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.claude/worktrees/sync-state-machine/custom_components/lock_code_manager/coordinator.py` is cleared in `_reset_backoff()`, which is called on both successful polls and push updates. This creates a clean recovery path.
- The Z-Wave `get_usercode_from_node` wrapping in `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.claude/worktrees/sync-state-machine/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py` correctly prevents raw `FailedZWaveCommand` from hitting the generic exception handler.
- Test coverage is thorough: 13 new state machine tests, 4 coordinator tests, 2 Z-Wave tests, plus updates to existing tests. All 634 tests pass in ~8 seconds.
- The `slot_suspended` repair issue with translations and fix flow is complete and consistent with the existing `slot_disabled` pattern.

### Issues Found

#### Important (should fix)

**1. Circuit breaker tracker not reset on sync-target transition**

The old code had explicit logic to reset the circuit breaker tracker when the tick detected a sync-target change (True-to-False or False-to-True transition via `_tick_in_sync`). This prevented stale attempt counts from a prior sync cycle from incorrectly triggering the breaker when, for example, a user changes the PIN while a prior sync cycle had accumulated attempts.

The new code removed this entirely. The only places `_reset_sync_tracker` is now called are: (a) `_suspend_lock`, (b) when transitioning to SYNCED, and (c) `_disable_slot`. There is no reset when the sync target changes (e.g., PIN edited while out-of-sync with accumulated attempts from a different PIN).

Consider this scenario: Slot is OUT_OF_SYNC trying to set PIN "1111", accumulates 2 of 3 attempts. User changes PIN to "2222". The state stays OUT_OF_SYNC (via `_request_sync_check`), but the 2 stale attempts from the "1111" cycle remain. One more failure on "2222" trips the breaker.

The old test `test_sync_tracker_resets_on_pin_change_in_tick` was renamed to `test_sync_tracker_does_not_fire_breaker_with_expired_window` and the test now only validates the expired-window path (setting `_sync_attempt_first` far in the past). This is a different scenario. The original test validated that a PIN change within the window resets the tracker -- that protection is now gone.

Mitigation: The SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW (5 minutes) provides some protection, and in practice a user changing a PIN while 2 attempts have failed within 5 minutes is unusual. But this is a behavioral regression worth considering.

**2. `_request_sync_check` does work in a `@callback`-decorated method**

`_request_sync_check` calls `_resolve_slot_state()` and `calculate_in_sync()` every time a coordinator update or state change fires. The old `_mark_dirty` just set `_dirty = True` (O(1)). The new approach does dictionary lookups, state resolution, and comparison on every event. For high-frequency coordinator updates, this could add CPU overhead in the event loop. This is unlikely to be a practical problem with typical lock counts, but worth noting.

**3. `_suspend_lock` is not an async method but `_disable_slot` is**

`_suspend_lock` at line 376 of `sync.py` creates a repair issue synchronously (which is fine -- `async_create_issue` is sync despite the name). However, the naming inconsistency between `_suspend_lock` (sync) and `_disable_slot` (async) could confuse future contributors. This is minor.

#### Suggestions (nice to have)

**4. Missing `_write_state()` after successful sync with `slot_disabled` issue cleanup**

At lines 639-653 of `sync.py`, when sync succeeds and the state transitions to SYNCED, `_write_state()` is called. But note that `_write_state()` happens before the `async_delete_issue` calls. If `async_delete_issue` raises (unlikely but possible), the state is already written as SYNCED. This is fine and consistent with the existing pattern -- just calling it out.

**5. LOADING state also deletes `slot_disabled_` issue on initial sync**

At lines 515-522 of `sync.py`, when LOADING transitions to SYNCED, the code deletes `slot_disabled_` issues but does not delete `slot_suspended_` issues. If a lock was suspended before a restart and comes back in sync, the suspended issue would persist until the next OUT_OF_SYNC -> SYNCED transition. Consider adding `slot_suspended_` cleanup in the LOADING -> SYNCED path as well.

**6. `sync_status` attribute translations do not include `"loading"`**

The `SyncState` enum has 5 values (LOADING, SYNCED, OUT_OF_SYNC, SYNCING, SUSPENDED), but the `strings.json` / `translations/en.json` state translations only include 4 (synced, out_of_sync, syncing, suspended). The `sync_status` property returns `None` for LOADING, which is correct since the binary sensor is unavailable at that point -- but if a future change exposes "loading" as a string value, the translation would be missing. This is a non-issue today given the `None` return.

**7. `_state` initialization should use `SyncState.LOADING` in `async_start` explicitly**

In `async_start()`, the `_dirty = True` was removed (correct since LOADING is the initial state), but it might be clearer to assert or set `self._state = SyncState.LOADING` in `async_start` to make the intent explicit at the lifecycle boundary. Currently, LOADING is set in `__init__` and relied upon implicitly.

**8. Design spec file not found in the repo**

The issue description references `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-20-sync-state-machine-design.md` but this file does not exist in the branch. This is likely a working document that was not committed (possibly intentional if specs are kept elsewhere), but worth confirming.

### Cross-file Consistency

- `ATTR_SYNC_STATUS` in `const.py` matches usage in `binary_sensor.py` -- correct.
- `SyncState` in `models.py` is imported consistently in `sync.py`, `conftest.py`, `test_binary_sensor.py`, `test_sync.py` -- correct.
- `coordinator.suspended` attribute added in `coordinator.py`, used in `sync.py`, tested in `test_coordinator.py` -- correct.
- `slot_suspended` translation key matches across `strings.json`, `translations/en.json`, `repairs.py`, and `sync.py` -- correct.
- Repair flow registration in `repairs.py` uses `startswith(("slot_disabled_", "pin_required_", "slot_suspended_"))` -- correct tuple form.

### Edge Cases in the State Machine

- **SYNCING state in tick gate**: `_async_tick` skips SYNCING, which is correct since only one tick can run at a time (single-threaded event loop). If somehow two ticks overlapped, the gate prevents re-entry.
- **LOADING + invalid active state**: Returns without state change, stays LOADING, will be picked up on next tick -- correct.
- **LOADING + `_resolve_slot_state` returns None**: Stays LOADING -- correct.
- **OUT_OF_SYNC + coordinator.suspended becomes True between ticks**: First thing `_async_tick_impl` checks after LOADING is `coordinator.suspended`, transitions to SUSPENDED -- correct.
- **CodeRejectedError sets state to OUT_OF_SYNC after disable**: This allows the next tick to see the disabled slot as in-sync and transition to SYNCED -- correct design.

### Test Coverage Assessment

Coverage is strong. The new `TestSyncStateMachine` class covers all key transitions:
- LOADING -> SYNCED, LOADING -> OUT_OF_SYNC
- SYNCED -> OUT_OF_SYNC
- OUT_OF_SYNC -> SYNCED (after sync)
- SYNCING -> OUT_OF_SYNC (LockDisconnected)
- SYNCING -> SUSPENDED (generic exception, circuit breaker)
- SUSPENDED -> OUT_OF_SYNC (recovery)
- SUSPENDED stays SUSPENDED (coordinator still suspended)
- CodeRejectedError still disables slot
- SUSPENDED skips tick

One gap: there is no test for **OUT_OF_SYNC -> SUSPENDED via `coordinator.suspended` being True** (the check at line 535). The `test_syncing_to_suspended_on_circuit_breaker` test validates the circuit breaker path, but the direct "coordinator already suspended when tick runs" path is not explicitly tested.

### Code Style Compliance

- No `nonlocal`/`local`/`global` usage -- compliant.
- No inline imports -- compliant.
- No Google-style Args/Returns docstrings -- compliant.
- Acronyms are spelled out in comments -- compliant.
- No caplog text assertions in new tests -- compliant.

### Summary

This is a well-executed refactor. The state machine is a significant improvement over the three-flag approach. The one item I would call out as worth discussing before merge is Issue #1 (circuit breaker tracker not being reset on sync-target change) and Issue #5 (missing `slot_suspended` cleanup in the LOADING -> SYNCED path). Everything else is solid.

This isolates lock failures per-lock instead of per-profile, so one unreachable lock no longer disables slots across all locks in the profile.\n\n**State machine states:** `LOADING` → `SYNCED` ↔ `OUT_OF_SYNC` → `SYNCING` → `SYNCED` | `OUT_OF_SYNC` | `SUSPENDED`\n\n**Key changes:**\n- **`SyncState` enum** (`LOADING`, `SYNCED`, `OUT_OF_SYNC`, `SYNCING`, `SUSPENDED`) replaces three boolean flags, making impossible states unrepresentable\n- **Per-lock suspension**: Circuit breaker and unexpected errors now set a `suspended` flag on the coordinator (per-lock scope) instead of calling `_disable_slot` (profile-wide scope). `CodeRejectedError`/`DuplicateCodeError` still disable the slot profile-wide since the code itself is bad.\n- **`sync_status` attribute** on the in-sync binary sensor: `synced`, `out_of_sync`, `syncing`, `suspended` — with translations for dashboard styling\n- **`slot_suspended` repair issue**: Per-lock repair issue created on suspension, auto-cleared on recovery\n- **Z-Wave error wrapping**: `get_usercode_from_node()` failures in V1 locks now raise `LockDisconnected` instead of leaking raw `FailedZWaveCommand`, routing them into the retry path\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [ ] Dependency upgrade\n- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)\n- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)\n- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)\n- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests\n\n## Additional information\n\n- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #1061\n- This PR is related to issue:\nEOF\n)\"",

## Combined Review Summary

All reviews agree the refactor is clean and well-structured. Here are the actionable findings across all sources:

### Bug: `_request_sync_check` resets circuit breaker on coordinator updates (Copilot + our earlier final review)

**Severity: HIGH** — This can prevent the circuit breaker from ever tripping.

The `OUT_OF_SYNC` branch in `_request_sync_check` unconditionally calls `_reset_sync_tracker()`. Since this callback is wired to coordinator updates too (not just entity state changes), every successful coordinator refresh resets `_sync_attempt_count`, wiping attempts between ticks.

**Fix**: Only reset the tracker when the *desired sync target* changes (PIN, active, name), not on coordinator updates. We need to distinguish entity state changes from coordinator updates, or compare a stored fingerprint.

### Important: Z-Wave `except Exception` is too broad (Copilot + Silent Failure Hunter)

**Severity: MEDIUM** — Both reviewers flagged this independently.

Catching bare `Exception` in `get_usercode_from_node` wraps programming errors (`TypeError`, `AttributeError`) as `LockDisconnected`, causing silent infinite retries instead of surfacing the bug via the suspension path.

**Fix**: Narrow the catch to the expected Z-Wave exceptions, or at minimum add a warning-level log.

### Minor: `"syncing"` translation is unreachable (Code reviewer)

`_write_state()` is never called when entering SYNCING (it's transient within a tick). The translation exists for dashboard flexibility but is currently dead code. Low priority — it enables future use without being harmful.

### Non-issues confirmed:
- `_reset_backoff` clearing `suspended` is **by design** — lock recovery is the resume signal
- Repair issue acknowledgment not resuming sync is **by design** — explained in the issue text
- Codecov: 96.46% patch coverage, 4 lines missing in sync.py — acceptable

---

Now let me implement all fixes. Starting with the analysis for fix #1:

The old code's `_tick_in_sync` only reset the tracker on *transitions* (True→False or False→True). It did NOT reset when staying OUT_OF_SYNC (False→False). So the OUT_OF_SYNC branch in `_request_sync_check` that unconditionally resets was wrong — it fires on every coordinator update. The fix is to remove that branch entirely. The IN_SYNC → OUT_OF_SYNC transition already resets (line 453), which covers the "sync target changed" case.

> AGENT

The issue is that patching `_perform_sync` to succeed means the mock lock's `async_internal_set_usercode` is never called, so the coordinator data doesn't get updated. But the mock lock already has code "1234" in slot 1, and the coordinator also has "1234" — so after the mocked sync, the post-sync check finds everything in sync.

The problem is: I set `coordinator.data[1] = SlotCode.EMPTY` to make it out of sync, but after `_perform_sync` (mocked as success), the code does `coordinator.async_refresh()` which re-fetches from the mock lock (which has "1234"). So the coordinator data gets refreshed back to "1234" and the post-sync check finds it in sync.

I need to also make `_resolve_slot_state` return an out-of-sync state *after* the sync. The simplest way: patch `calculate_in_sync` to return `False` after sync:

In `_request_sync_check`, the `OUT_OF_SYNC` branch unconditionally calls `_reset_sync_tracker()`. Because this callback is also wired to coordinator updates (`_setup_coordinator_listener`), every successful coordinator refresh will reset `_sync_attempt_count` even if nothing about the desired target (PIN/active) changed. Since `DataUpdateCoordinator` notifies listeners on each refresh, this can prevent the circuit breaker from ever tripping (attempts get wiped between ticks). Consider only resetting the tracker when the desired sync target changes (e.g., PIN/active/name change), and avoid resetting on coordinator-driven updates (split callbacks or compare a stored “desired state” fingerprint before resetting).
`get_usercode_from_node()` failures are wrapped by catching `Exception`, which will also convert unexpected programming/data errors (e.g., bad slot number, attribute errors) into `LockDisconnected` and route them into the retry path. To avoid masking real bugs and causing indefinite retries, narrow the except clause to the Z-Wave communication exceptions you expect here (e.g., `zwave_js_server.exceptions.FailedZWaveCommand` / relevant Z-Wave JS exceptions) and re-raise others.
Same as above in `async_clear_usercode`: catching `Exception` here will treat non-connection errors as `LockDisconnected` and keep retrying. Prefer catching only the expected Z-Wave communication failure types from `get_usercode_from_node()` and letting other exceptions propagate so they can be surfaced/fixed.
`_reset_backoff()` now unconditionally sets `self.suspended = False`. Since `coordinator.suspended` is also used for the sync state machine’s circuit breaker / unexpected-error suspension, clearing it on any successful poll/push update can prematurely resume syncing even when the underlying sync failure hasn’t been resolved (e.g., lock reachable but silently rejecting codes), potentially causing repeated suspend/resume cycles and noisy repair issue churn. Consider separating “connectivity recovered” from “sync suspended” (separate flags/reason), or only clearing `suspended` when it was set by the coordinator’s own backoff path.
```suggestion
        flag and stop retrying until the sync failure is explicitly
        handled by the code path that suspended syncing.
        """
        self._suspended = True

    def _reset_backoff(self) -> None:
        """Reset polling failure state and restore original update interval."""
```

1. **MEDIUM:** `_request_sync_check` stays IN_SYNC when `_resolve_slot_state` returns None — acceptable since recovery happens on next event (same behavior as old code)
2. **LOW:** No debug log distinguishing post-sync "state unresolvable" vs "still mismatched"
3. **LOW:** SYNCING state never written to HA (translation is dead code) — we discussed this earlier, kept intentionally for future flexibility
4. **LOW:** Per-lock repair issue key means last-suspending slot overwrites prior reason — by design since suspension is per-lock

**Test Coverage Analyzer:** No critical gaps. Three minor suggestions (5-6 importance):
1. Test OUT_OF_SYNC tick entering SUSPENDED via coordinator.suspended (cross-manager propagation)
2. Test `_request_sync_check` no-op for LOADING/SYNCING states
3. Assert `_state is OUT_OF_SYNC` after CodeRejectedError in existing test

**Copilot:** No new review yet (only the old one from round 1, which we already addressed).

### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:529
`slot_suspended_...` is a per-lock repair issue, but it’s only deleted when `active_state == STATE_ON`. If all slots for the lock are disabled (or this slot is OFF), the suspension issue may never auto-clear even after recovery. Consider deleting the per-lock `slot_suspended_...` issue whenever the lock is no longer suspended / state becomes `IN_SYNC`, regardless of the slot’s active state.
```suggestion
                async_delete_issue(
                    self._hass,
                    DOMAIN,
                    f"slot_suspended_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._lock.lock.entity_id}",
                )
```
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:562
Same as above: per-lock `slot_suspended_...` issue cleanup is gated on `active_state == STATE_ON`, which can leave a stale repair issue if all slots are OFF/disabled when the lock recovers. Per-lock issues should generally clear independent of any one slot being enabled.
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:660
Same as above: the per-lock `slot_suspended_...` issue is only deleted when `active_state == STATE_ON`. This can prevent auto-clear on recovery for locks where all slots are currently disabled. Consider removing the `STATE_ON` guard for the per-lock issue deletion.
```suggestion
            async_delete_issue(
                self._hass,
                DOMAIN,
                f"slot_suspended_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._lock.lock.entity_id}",
            )
```
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:399
`_suspend_lock()` creates a persistent `slot_suspended_{entry_id}_{lock_entity_id}` repair issue, but the integration’s unload cleanup (see `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py` slot issue deletion loop) currently only deletes `slot_disabled_` and `pin_required_`. This new issue may be left behind if the config entry is removed/unloaded while suspended. Consider adding unload-time cleanup for `slot_suspended_...` issues (or making them non-persistent if appropriate).
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:609
`SyncState.SYNCING` is set but never written via `_write_state()`, so the new `sync_status` attribute likely never reports `"syncing"` to Home Assistant. If the intent is to expose a "syncing" UI state (translations were added), consider calling `_write_state()` when entering `SYNCING` and also when transitioning back to `OUT_OF_SYNC` on handled failures so the attribute updates deterministically.
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/binary_sensor.py:281
`extra_state_attributes` always returns `{sync_status: None}` when the manager is still LOADING. It’s usually cleaner to omit attributes whose value is `None` to avoid exposing nulls in state and to reduce unnecessary state changes.
```suggestion
    def extra_state_attributes(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Return extra state attributes."""
        if self._attr_sync_status is None:
            return {}
```
---
### tests/test_sync.py:457
This docstring refers to “SYNCED”, but the state enum uses `IN_SYNC`. Consider updating the terminology for consistency with `SyncState` and `sync_status` values.
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/coordinator.py:178
`LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator.suspend()` sets `_suspended=True` but does not notify DataUpdateCoordinator listeners. SlotSyncManagers that are currently `IN_SYNC` won't tick (and won’t transition to `SUSPENDED`), so suspension won’t propagate across all slots for the lock. Consider calling `async_update_listeners()` (or otherwise notifying listeners) when suspending so all per-slot managers can update their state/UI promptly.
---
### tests/test_sync.py:441
The docstring says “SYNCED” but the state name used throughout the code/tests is `IN_SYNC`. Updating the wording here (and in similar docstrings below) would avoid confusion when reading test failures.
---

4. **Stale "SYNCED" in docstrings** — easy fix.
5. **`extra_state_attributes` returning None** — cleaner to omit.

**Not actionable (by design):**

```
## Proposed change

Replaces the three independent boolean flags (`_dirty`, `_in_sync`, `_tick_in_sync`) in `SlotSyncManager` with an explicit `SyncState` enum state machine. This isolates lock failures per-lock instead of per-profile, so one unreachable lock no longer disables slots across all locks in the profile.

**State machine states:** `LOADING` → `SYNCED` ↔ `OUT_OF_SYNC` → `SYNCING` → `SYNCED` | `OUT_OF_SYNC` | `SUSPENDED`

**Key changes:**
- **`SyncState` enum** (`LOADING`, `SYNCED`, `OUT_OF_SYNC`, `SYNCING`, `SUSPENDED`) replaces three boolean flags, making impossible states unrepresentable
- **Per-lock suspension**: Circuit breaker and unexpected errors now set a `suspended` flag on the coordinator (per-lock scope) instead of calling `_disable_slot` (profile-wide scope). `CodeRejectedError`/`DuplicateCodeError` still disable the slot profile-wide since the code itself is bad.
- **`sync_status` attribute** on the in-sync binary sensor: `synced`, `out_of_sync`, `syncing`, `suspended` — with translations for dashboard styling
- **`slot_suspended` repair issue**: Per-lock repair issue created on suspension, auto-cleared on recovery
- **Z-Wave error wrapping**: `get_usercode_from_node()` failures in V1 locks now raise `LockDisconnected` instead of leaking raw `FailedZWaveCommand`, routing them into the retry path

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #1061
- This PR is related to issue:
```

### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:454
`_request_sync_check` is a no-op while already in OUT_OF_SYNC, so if the desired sync target (e.g., PIN/name/active) changes again before the slot returns to IN_SYNC, the existing `_sync_attempt_count` carries over and can trip the circuit breaker for a *new* target. Consider resetting the sync-attempt tracker (or tracking a “current target” fingerprint) on relevant state changes even when `_state` is OUT_OF_SYNC.
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:587
`SyncState.SYNCING` is set here, but the manager never calls `_write_state()` for this transition. Because `in_sync` remains False in both OUT_OF_SYNC and SYNCING, the binary sensor likely won’t ever surface `sync_status="syncing"` (attribute will stay at the prior value). Consider writing state whenever `_state` changes (even when `in_sync` doesn’t) so `sync_status` remains accurate.
```suggestion
        self._state = SyncState.SYNCING
        self._write_state()
```
---
### custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py:621
The broad `except Exception` will also catch `asyncio.CancelledError` during unload/shutdown and convert it into a lock suspension + repair issue. Home Assistant generally expects cancellations to propagate. Consider adding an explicit `except CancelledError: raise` (or otherwise letting cancellations bubble up) before the generic handler.
---
```

> AGENT

Three comments:

1. **Circuit breaker carries over when target changes while OUT_OF_SYNC** — We discussed this earlier. The old code had the same behavior (no reset on OUT_OF_SYNC → OUT_OF_SYNC). The 5-minute window provides natural expiry. Not fixing.

2. **SYNCING never written to HA** — Discussed multiple times. Intentional — it's transient within a single tick. Not fixing.

3. **`asyncio.CancelledError` caught by generic `except Exception`** — This is a real issue! In Python 3.9+, `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it won't be caught by `except Exception`. But in older Python, it was an `Exception` subclass. Let me verify what Python version this runs on.

> AGENT

Good question — on Python 3.13+ it technically can't, since `CancelledError` is a `BaseException` and `except Exception` won't catch it. The explicit `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise` is purely defensive — it documents the intent ("we know cancellation should propagate") and protects against:

1. Future Python changes (unlikely but possible)
2. Someone adding `except BaseException` during refactoring
3. Making the intent explicit for readers of the code

If you'd rather not have dead code, I can remove it. It's a style call — some projects add it as a defensive pattern, others consider it noise.

> DEVELOPER

we can remove it - I mean more that, in what scenarios does CancelledError actually occur that matter to us

> AGENT

You're right — `CancelledError` would only fire here if `_perform_sync` (which calls `async_internal_set_usercode` / `async_internal_clear_usercode`) gets cancelled. That happens during HA shutdown or config entry unload, which already tears down the sync manager via `async_stop` (unsubscribes the tick timer). So by the time shutdown cancels tasks, the tick isn't running anymore.

The only edge case would be if someone calls `config_entry.async_cancel_task()` on the tick mid-execution, but that's not a pattern used anywhere in this codebase.

So it's not a real concern. Let me revert.

> DEVELOPER

is there harm in writing syncing to state?

> AGENT

No real harm — `_write_state()` just calls `self._state_writer(self.in_sync)` which triggers `async_write_ha_state()`. Since `in_sync` is `False` for both OUT_OF_SYNC and SYNCING, the binary sensor's `is_on` won't change. The only effect is the `sync_status` attribute flipping from `"out_of_sync"` to `"syncing"` for the duration of the await.

The downside is minor: one extra HA state write per sync attempt (and another when transitioning out of SYNCING). For a 5-second tick that's negligible. The upside is the dashboard could show a spinner or different color while actively syncing, which is the whole reason we added the translation.

I've completed a thorough search of the Lock Code Manager codebase for dashboard card/strategy code and references to the in-sync binary sensor. Here are my findings:

### Current In-Sync Data Flow

**Backend (`binary_sensor.py`):**
- The `LockCodeManagerCodeSlotInSyncEntity` class has an attribute `_attr_sync_status` (line 253)
- Extra state attributes are returned via the `extra_state_attributes` property (lines 280-284), which includes `ATTR_SYNC_STATUS: self._attr_sync_status` when set
- The sync status is managed by `SlotSyncManager` and assigned to `self._attr_sync_status` (line 259)

**Backend (`websocket.py`):**
- The `_build_lock_status()` function (lines 739-788) builds the lock status dict that's sent to the frontend

**Frontend (`slot-card.ts`):**

### Update Required

**YES, the card NEEDS updating to support the new `sync_status` extra state attribute.** Here's what needs to happen:

1. **Backend (`websocket.py`):**
   - Modify `_build_lock_status()` to read `sync_status` from the in_sync binary sensor's extra state attributes
   - Add logic to extract the value from `hass.states[in_sync_entity_id].attributes.get('sync_status')`

2. **Frontend (TypeScript):**

   - Add `syncStatus?: string` field to internal `LockSyncStatus` interface in `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/ts/slot-card.ts` (around line 42)
   - Update `_renderLockRow()` to display the sync_status value when available (potentially as additional context or detail text)
   - Update data mapping in `_renderFromData()` to pass the sync_status from incoming data

The dashboard card currently only uses the boolean `in_sync` state and `last_synced` timestamp, but the infrastructure for `sync_status` extra attribute support already exists on the backend (defined in binary_sensor.py). The missing piece is retrieving and forwarding that attribute value to the frontend through the WebSocket API.

> AGENT

The card currently displays "Synced", "Pending", or "Unknown" based on the boolean `in_sync` state. It doesn't read extra state attributes — the data flows through the WebSocket API (`websocket.py` → `slot-card.ts`).

**To support `sync_status`, two things need updating:**
1. `websocket.py` — add `sync_status` to the lock status dict sent to the frontend
2. `slot-card.ts` — add the field to types and use it in rendering (e.g., show "Suspended" instead of generic "Pending")

**But it won't break without these changes.** The card will continue showing "Pending" for any non-synced state (OUT_OF_SYNC, SYNCING, and SUSPENDED all map to `in_sync = False`). Users just won't see the granular distinction until the card is updated.

Want me to create an issue for the card enhancement, or leave it for later?

## Exploration Report: Lock Code Manager TypeScript Frontend

### 1. **SlotCardLockStatus Type** — WebSocket Response Mapping

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/ts/types.ts` (Lines 200-211)

```typescript
export interface SlotCardLockStatus {
    /** Code on the lock: actual PIN, null, "empty" (cleared), or "unreadable_code" (unreadable) */
    code: string | null;
    /** Code length when masked (readable code, not revealed) */
    code_length?: number;
    entity_id: string;
    /** Whether code is synced to lock */
    in_sync: boolean;
    /** Last sync timestamp (ISO) */
    last_synced?: string;
    name: string;
}
```

**Key properties:**
- `in_sync: boolean` — Sync status from backend (true = synced, false = pending, null/undefined = unknown)
- `last_synced?: string` — ISO timestamp of last successful sync
- `code` & `code_length` — For displaying the actual code on the lock (separate from configured PIN)

This interface is used in `SlotCardData` as an array: `locks: SlotCardLockStatus[]` (line 296)

---

### 2. **_renderLockRow() Method** — Sync Status Rendering

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/ts/slot-card.ts` (Lines 936-1002)

**Location:** `LockCodeManagerSlotCard` class, private method

**Sync Status Logic (Lines 945-954):**
```typescript
let iconClass: string;
let statusText: string;

if (lock.inSync === true) {
    iconClass = 'synced';
    statusText = 'Synced';
} else if (lock.inSync === false) {
    iconClass = 'pending';
    statusText = 'Pending';
} else {
    iconClass = 'unknown';
    statusText = 'Unknown';
}
```

**HTML Rendering (Lines 960-985):**
- Uses `mdi:check-circle` icon with class `.lcm-sync-icon ${iconClass}`
- Displays `statusText` ("Synced", "Pending", "Unknown") in `.lock-synced-time` span
- Shows `last_synced` as relative time when available: `Last synced to lock <ha-relative-time>`
- Falls back to status text if no `lastSynced` timestamp

}

### 5. **Color & Icon Scheme for Sync States**

**Icons:** `mdi:check-circle` (single icon for all states, color changes via class)

**Colors (from shared-styles.ts, lines 105-120):**

| Sync State | Icon Class | Color CSS Variable | Actual Color | Hex Code |
|------------|------------|-------------------|--------------|----------|
| Synced    | `.synced`   | `--lcm-success-color` | `var(--success-color, #4caf50)` | Green |
| Pending   | `.pending`  | `--lcm-warning-color` | `var(--warning-color, #ff9800)` | Orange |
| Unknown   | `.unknown`  | `--lcm-disabled-color` | `var(--disabled-text-color, #9e9e9e)` | Gray |

**CSS class application (shared-styles.ts, lines 106-120):**
```typescript
.lcm-sync-icon {
    --mdc-icon-size: 18px;
}

.lcm-sync-icon.synced {
    color: var(--lcm-success-color);      /* Green */
}

.lcm-sync-icon.pending {
    color: var(--lcm-warning-color);      /* Orange */
}

.lcm-sync-icon.unknown {
    color: var(--lcm-disabled-color);     /* Gray */
}
```

**CSS Variables Definition (shared-styles.ts, lines 13-53):**
- All colors inherit from Home Assistant theme CSS variables
- Can be customized via `--lcm-success-color`, `--lcm-warning-color`, `--lcm-disabled-color`
- Fallback to defaults if HA theme variables not available

- Collapsible badge showing sync count: `${syncedCount}/${totalCount}` (slot-card.ts, line 919)
- Status dot styling available in `.lcm-status-dot` (shared-styles.ts, lines 122-138) with similar color scheme

523	async def subscribe_lock_codes(
524	    hass: HomeAssistant,
525	    connection: websocket_api.ActiveConnection,
526	    msg: dict[str, Any],
527	) -> None:
528	    """
529	    Subscribe to coordinator data and LCM entity state updates for a lock.
530	
531	    Triggers updates when:
532	    - Lock coordinator data changes (codes on lock)
533	    - LCM entity states change (enabled, active, name, configured PIN)
534	    """
535	    lock_entity_id = msg[ATTR_LOCK_ENTITY_ID]
536	    reveal = msg["reveal"]
537	    lock = hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(CONF_LOCKS, {}).get(lock_entity_id)
538	    if not lock:
539	        connection.send_error(
540	            msg["id"],
541	            websocket_api.const.ERR_NOT_FOUND,
542	            f"Lock {lock_entity_id} is not managed by Lock Code Manager",
543	        )
544	        return
545	
546	    coordinator = lock.coordinator
547	
548	    # Mutable container for the current state tracking unsubscribe callback,
549	    # allowing it to be replaced when tracked entities change
550	    unsub_state_ref: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
551	    tracked_set: set[str] = set()
552	
553	    @callback
554	    def _refresh_lock_state_tracking() -> None:
555	        """Re-subscribe to state changes if the tracked entity set has changed."""
556	        new_ids = set(_get_slot_state_entity_ids(hass, lock_entity_id))
557	        if new_ids == tracked_set:
558	            return
559	        tracked_set.clear()
560	        tracked_set.update(new_ids)
561	        # Unsubscribe from previous tracking
562	        if unsub_state_ref:
563	            unsub_state_ref[0]()
564	            unsub_state_ref.clear()
565	        # Subscribe to new set
566	        if new_ids:
567	            unsub_state_ref.append(
568	                async_track_state_change_event(hass, list(new_ids), _on_state_change)
569	            )
570	
571	    @callback
572	    def _send_update() -> None:
573	        connection.send_event(
574	            msg["id"], _serialize_lock_coordinator(hass, lock, reveal=reveal)
575	        )
576	        # Re-resolve tracked entities to pick up entities created after
577	        # subscription was established
578	        _refresh_lock_state_tracking()
579	
580	    @callback
581	    def _on_state_change(event: Event[EventStateChangedData]) -> None:
582	        """Handle Lock Code Manager entity state changes."""
583	        old_state = event.data.get("old_state")
584	        new_state = event.data.get("new_state")
585	
586	        # Only send update if actual state value changed or entity created/removed
587	        if old_state is None or new_state is None or old_state.state != new_state.state:
588	            _send_update()
589	
590	    # Track coordinator updates (lock code changes).
591	    unsub_coordinator = (
592	        coordinator.async_add_listener(_send_update) if coordinator else lambda: None
593	    )
594	
595	    # Track Lock Code Manager entity state changes (enabled, active, name, PIN)
596	    slot_entity_ids = _get_slot_state_entity_ids(hass, lock_entity_id)
597	    tracked_set.update(slot_entity_ids)
598	    if slot_entity_ids:
599	        unsub_state_ref.append(
600	            async_track_state_change_event(hass, slot_entity_ids, _on_state_change)
601	        )
602	
603	    def _unsub_all() -> None:
604	        unsub_coordinator()
605	        if unsub_state_ref:
606	            unsub_state_ref[0]()
607	
608	    connection.subscriptions[msg["id"]] = _unsub_all
609	    connection.send_result(msg["id"])
610	    _send_update()

Now I have the full picture. Here's what I need to do:

1. **`types.ts`**: Add `sync_status?: string` to `SlotCardLockStatus` 
2. **`slot-card.ts`**: Add `syncStatus` to `LockSyncStatus`, pass it in the mapping, use it in `_renderLockRow`
3. **`lock-codes-card.ts`**: The lock-codes card uses a different websocket (`subscribe_lock_codes`) that returns per-slot data. It doesn't have per-lock sync status. For the lock card, we'd need to add a lock-level `sync_suspended` field to `_serialize_lock_coordinator`. But let me scope this to what we already have — the slot card already gets `sync_status` per lock.
4. **Styling**: Add `suspended` icon class with appropriate color and icon

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The slot card gets per-lock sync status via `subscribe_slot_data` → `_build_lock_status()`. The lock-codes card gets per-slot data via `subscribe_lock_codes` → `_serialize_lock_coordinator()`. To show suspension on the lock-codes card, we'd need to add `slot_sync_mgrs_suspended` to the lock-level data in `_serialize_lock_coordinator`. Let me add that too.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Let me implement this. I'll present the design choice for suspension styling to you:

For the **slot card**, each lock row currently shows an icon + status text. With `sync_status`, we can show:
- `in_sync` → green check, "Synced" (same as now)
- `out_of_sync` → orange clock, "Out of sync"
- `syncing` → orange sync-rotating icon, "Syncing"  
- `suspended` → red alert icon, "Suspended"

For the **lock-codes card**, we could add a banner/badge at the top of the card when `slot_sync_mgrs_suspended` is true, something like a warning bar: "Sync suspended — lock is unreachable".

Does this direction work, or do you want something different?

482	) -> dict[str, Any]:
483	    """Serialize coordinator data for a lock."""
484	    coordinator = lock.coordinator
485	    data = coordinator.data if coordinator is not None else {}
486	    managed_slots = get_managed_slots(hass, lock.lock.entity_id)
487	    slot_metadata = _get_slot_metadata(hass, lock.lock.entity_id)

504	                config_entry_id=slot_ids.config_entry_id if slot_ids else None,
505	            )

---

## PR #1063 Review: Zigbee2MQTT Lock Provider

### Critical Issues

**1. `setup_push_subscription` violates the synchronous `@callback` contract** (Code Reviewer, Confidence: 95)

The base class defines `setup_push_subscription` as `@callback` (synchronous). The Z2M implementation uses `hass.async_create_task(_async_subscribe())` and returns immediately. This means:
- `_unsubscribe` is still `None` on return — idempotency guard is broken, rapid reconnects spawn duplicate subscriptions
- The caller expects push is active on return — it isn't, and failures are swallowed
- Matches Silent Failure Hunter Issue #3 (subscription failure swallowed by fire-and-forget task)

**2. Timeout in `async_get_usercodes` returns `SlotCode.EMPTY` instead of signaling failure** (Silent Failure Hunter, Confidence: HIGH)

A timeout means "we don't know" not "the slot is empty." Combined with the optimistic `push_update` in set operations, this creates a dangerous scenario:
1. Lock goes offline → get times out → coordinator sees all slots "empty"
2. Sync manager re-pushes codes → publish "succeeds" (to broker) → coordinator marks as set
3. Lock is still offline, messages dropped → state diverges silently until next hard refresh

Should raise `LockDisconnected` (or the coordinator equivalent) on timeout.

**3. `call_soon_threadsafe` is unnecessary** (Code Reviewer, Confidence: 82)

HA's MQTT callbacks already run on the event loop. The extra scheduling hop is unnecessary and adds latency.

### High Severity

**4. `async_set_usercode`/`async_clear_usercode` wrap ALL exceptions as `LockDisconnected`** (Both reviewers)

Broad `except Exception` converts programming errors, auth failures, etc. into transient "disconnected" — causing infinite retries of permanent failures. Should narrow to MQTT-specific exceptions.

**5. Optimistic `push_update` without delivery confirmation** (Silent Failure Hunter)

MQTT QoS 0 provides no delivery guarantee. The coordinator is told "code is set" when it's only been handed to the broker. Security concern for a lock manager.

**6. `async_is_integration_connected` conflates device availability with integration connectivity** (Code Reviewer, Confidence: 85)

Entity state "unavailable" check belongs in `async_is_device_available`, not `async_is_integration_connected`. Per base class contract.

**7. Missing `@callback` decorators on push subscription methods** (Code Reviewer, Confidence: 88)

**8. No `async_fire_code_slot_event` for lock/unlock actions** (Code Reviewer, Confidence: 82)

README claims "Code Events: Yes" but PIN-used events aren't fired.

### Medium Severity

**9. Silent JSON parse failure with no logging** (Silent Failure Hunter)
**10. Invalid user IDs silently skipped** — should at least log at debug (Silent Failure Hunter)
**11. pin_code response parse failure causes invisible timeout** (Silent Failure Hunter)

---

### Recommendation

Issues #1 and #2 are blocking — they'll cause real production failures (duplicate subscriptions, false "empty" slots triggering unwanted code pushes). The provider needs architectural changes to handle MQTT's async subscribe within the synchronous `@callback` contract, and timeout handling needs to signal failure rather than assume empty.

At minimum, add a comment acknowledging the risk and how `hard_refresh_interval` mitigates it. Ideally, don't call `push_update` and let the next push/poll cycle confirm.\n\n**6. `async_is_integration_connected` conflates device availability with integration connectivity**\n\nThe entity state \"unavailable\" check belongs in `async_is_device_available()`, not `async_is_integration_connected()`. The "last synced" test passes because it checks `not.toContain('Last synced to lock')` which IS a static string. I need to check `result.values` for the dynamic parts:

I now have a complete picture. Here is my analysis:

---

## What's NOT Abstracted That Should Be

### 1. `_get_managed_slots()` helper method — Schlage and Akuvox

Both Schlage (`schlage.py:65-67`) and Akuvox (`akuvox.py:173-175`) define an identical single-line wrapper method:

```python
def _get_managed_slots(self) -> set[int]:
    return get_managed_slots(self.hass, self.lock.entity_id)
```

ZWaveJS (`zwave_js.py:526`) and Matter (`matter.py:427`) and Virtual (`virtual.py:105`) all call `get_managed_slots(self.hass, self.lock.entity_id)` inline without the wrapper. The wrapped form is marginally nicer to read but the wrapper itself is trivial enough it could live on `BaseLock` as a `@final` convenience property/method so all providers use it uniformly. Currently it's duplicated in two providers and inlined in three others.

**Proposed change:** Add to `BaseLock`:
```python
@final
def get_managed_slots(self) -> set[int]:
    return get_managed_slots(self.hass, self.lock.entity_id)
```

---

### 2. Optimistic `coordinator.push_update()` after set/clear — ZWaveJS and Matter

Both ZWaveJS and Matter follow the same pattern at the end of `async_set_usercode` and `async_clear_usercode`:

```python
if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data is not None:  # (Matter)
    self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: <value>})
# or
if self.coordinator:  # (ZWaveJS)
    self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: <value>})
```

This is the "optimistic update for push-based providers" pattern, documented in `_base.py:743-747`. The base class already knows that push-based providers should do this — the comment in `async_internal_set_usercode` explicitly says "Skip for push-based providers — they update the coordinator optimistically via push_update()." The base class even checks `not self.supports_push` to decide whether to call `coordinator.async_request_refresh()`.

So `BaseLock` already understands the distinction but requires providers to re-implement the optimistic push_update boilerplate themselves. If the base class performed the optimistic update for push-based providers automatically (using a return value from `async_set_usercode`/`async_clear_usercode` to indicate the resolved value), this pattern could be centralized. However, the resolved value differs between providers (plain string, `SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE`, `SlotCode.EMPTY`) and ZWaveJS sometimes skips it based on cc version logic, so the current design is intentional but results in copy-pasted guard code.

The guard pattern `if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data is not None` versus `if self.coordinator` is also inconsistent between Matter and ZWaveJS — Matter adds the `coordinator.data is not None` check, ZWaveJS does not. This is a subtle divergence with no documented reason.

---

### 3. Idempotent `teardown_push_subscription` pattern — ZWaveJS and Matter

Both ZWaveJS (`zwave_js.py:289-292`) and Matter (`matter.py:258-261`) implement teardown with the exact same pattern:

```python
def teardown_push_subscription(self) -> None:
    if self._event_unsub:
        self._event_unsub()
        self._event_unsub = None
```

This is unavoidable at the instance level since providers own their own unsub callables, but the idiom (null check, call, set to None) is identical. This can't easily be abstracted further without introducing a base-class-managed list of unsub callables — which is exactly what ZWaveJS already does with `_listeners` for its HA event listeners. ZWaveJS uses two different patterns for its own subscriptions: `_listeners: list[Callable[[], None]]` for HA bus listeners and `_value_update_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None` for the node value listener, with separate teardown logic for each.

---

### 4. `async_is_device_available()` check-via-fetch pattern — Matter and Schlage

Both Matter (`matter.py:205-219`) and Schlage (`schlage.py:127-138`) implement `async_is_device_available()` by calling their primary read service and catching exceptions:

```python
async def async_is_device_available(self) -> bool:
    try:
        await self._async_call_service("get_lock_info", {...})  # Matter
        # or
        await self._async_get_codes()  # Schlage
    except LockCodeManagerProviderError as err:
        LOGGER.debug("Lock %s: availability check failed: %s", ...)
        return False
    return True
```

This is a legitimate variation (different calls needed per provider), but the structural pattern — catch a provider error, log it at debug, return False — is identical. A base class helper like `_check_available_via(coro) -> bool` could reduce the boilerplate, though it's a minor case.

---

### 5. Service-call error wrapping — Akuvox and Schlage

Schlage and Akuvox both have `_async_add_code`/`_async_delete_code` and `_async_add_user`/`_async_delete_user` helper methods that:
1. Call `self.hass.services.async_call(...)` directly (bypassing `BaseLock.async_call_service`)
2. Wrap `HomeAssistantError` in `LockDisconnected`

Schlage (`schlage.py:101-110`, `schlage.py:115-125`) and Akuvox (`akuvox.py:115-128`, `akuvox.py:144-155`, `akuvox.py:161-171`) both duplicate this wrapping idiom. Meanwhile, `BaseLock.async_call_service` already does this wrapping (`_base.py:812-831`) — but it can't handle `ServiceValidationError` as a non-`LockDisconnected` case (which Matter needs) and doesn't support the `target` parameter pattern Akuvox uses.

Schlage's `_async_add_code` and `_async_delete_code` are candidates to be rewritten using `self.async_call_service()` directly — the `async_call_service` base method already handles `HomeAssistantError` → `LockDisconnected` wrapping. Akuvox also calls `hass.services.async_call` directly in `_async_add_user`, `_async_modify_user`, and `_async_delete_user` (all using `target=`) even though `async_call_service` in the base supports `target`.

Checking `_base.py:797-831`: `async_call_service` accepts `target: dict[str, Any] | None`. So Akuvox's three raw service call methods could use `self.async_call_service()` instead of calling `self.hass.services.async_call()` directly. Schlage's add/delete helpers could too. This is a missed opportunity to use the existing base-class abstraction.

---

### 6. `async_hard_refresh_codes()` pattern — Schlage and Akuvox

Both Schlage (`schlage.py:394-401`) and Akuvox (`akuvox.py:182-185`) implement `async_hard_refresh_codes` with the same two-step pattern: re-tag unmanaged codes/users, then call `async_get_usercodes()`. The structure is identical:

```python
async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:
    await self._async_tag_unmanaged_{codes/users}()
    return await self.async_get_usercodes()
```

These providers share the name-tagging abstraction via `_util.py`. The refresh pattern following from setup being `tag + get` is architecturally shared but cannot easily be collapsed into the base class since the tag step is provider-specific.

---

### 7. ZWaveJS `_listeners` list pattern is inconsistent with its own push-unsub field

ZWaveJS manages HA event listeners in `_listeners: list[Callable[[], None]]` (cleared and rebuilt in `async_setup`) and its node value listener in `_value_update_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None` (managed in `setup_push_subscription`/`teardown_push_subscription`). These are two parallel subscription-tracking mechanisms within one provider. The HA event listener could use the same pattern as the push unsub, or vice versa — instead, teardown requires two different code paths (`async_unload` iterates `_listeners`, `teardown_push_subscription` nulls out `_value_update_unsub`).

---

## What IS Abstracted That Shouldn't Be (or Is Unnecessarily Verbose)

### 1. `supports_code_slot_events` — ZWaveJS and Matter both return `True` (the default)

The base class defines `supports_code_slot_events` defaulting to `True` (`_base.py:375`). Both `ZWaveJSLock` (`zwave_js.py:127-129`) and `MatterLock` (`matter.py:68-70`) override it to return `True` — the same as the default. These overrides add no value and should be deleted. This creates visual noise and makes it appear as if these providers are making a meaningful choice when they are simply restating the default.

ZWaveJS's override:
```python
@property
def supports_code_slot_events(self) -> bool:
    """Return whether this lock supports code slot events."""
    return True
```

This is entirely redundant.

---

### 2. `domain` — required but not abstracted, has no default

`domain` uses `raise NotImplementedError()` (the bare Python version, not `self._raise_not_implemented()`) at `_base.py:325`. This is inconsistent with all other unimplemented methods (`async_set_usercode`, `async_clear_usercode`, etc.) which call `self._raise_not_implemented()`. Additionally, `domain` is a constant string on every provider — it could be a class variable rather than a `@property`, saving a small amount of boilerplate. The current design forces each provider to declare a `@property` that returns a string constant, where a `domain: ClassVar[str]` class variable would be cleaner and statically verifiable.

---

### 3. `setup_push_subscription`/`teardown_push_subscription` raise `ProviderNotImplementedError` by default

These default implementations raise on non-push providers. But `subscribe_push_updates` (the `@final` method) already checks for `ProviderNotImplementedError` and re-raises it. The caller (`BaseLock`) only calls `subscribe_push_updates()` when `supports_push is True`. So a non-push provider would only hit this path if it incorrectly set `supports_push = True` without overriding `setup_push_subscription` — which is a programming error, not a runtime error. The error would surface immediately on first setup.

However, the `teardown_push_subscription` default also raises `ProviderNotImplementedError`. `unsubscribe_push_updates` calls `teardown_push_subscription()` unconditionally without catching `ProviderNotImplementedError`. Checking `_base.py:423-427`:

```python
@final
@callback
def unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
    """Unsubscribe from push-based value updates."""
    self.teardown_push_subscription()
```

No exception handling here. And `teardown_push_subscription` raises by default. But `async_unload` calls `self.unsubscribe_push_updates()` only when `self.supports_push` is True (`_base.py:586-587`), so this won't fire on poll-only providers — it's safe. But the asymmetry between `subscribe_push_updates` (catches `ProviderNotImplementedError` and re-raises) and `unsubscribe_push_updates` (no catching) is a silent hazard.

---

### 4. `usercode_scan_interval` — three different values, all provider-specific

The base default is `timedelta(minutes=1)`. Schlage overrides to 5 minutes, Akuvox to 2 minutes, Matter to 5 minutes. ZWaveJS and Virtual use the default (ZWaveJS doesn't poll at all since it uses push, and Virtual has no latency concern). The variations are legitimate: each provider's API has different latency and rate-limit characteristics. This is a correct use of provider-specific configuration.

---

### 5. `async_is_integration_connected` for VirtualLock

VirtualLock (`virtual.py:58-60`) overrides `async_is_integration_connected` to always return `True`. The base class default checks `lock_config_entry.state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED`. A virtual lock has no real config entry to check, so the override is correct. However, the base default would return `False` for a `None` `lock_config_entry` (which virtual locks have), meaning the default behavior would permanently block all operations. The override is necessary.

But this reveals that the base class `async_is_integration_connected` has a surprising behavior: if `lock_config_entry` is `None`, the lock is treated as always disconnected. Virtual locks are the only case where `lock_config_entry` is `None` by design. There's no documentation in `BaseLock` explaining this edge case or that "if your provider doesn't have a lock config entry, override `async_is_integration_connected` to return True."

---

### Should move to base (repeated across providers)

| Pattern | Providers | Proposed Change |
|---|---|---|
| `get_managed_slots(self.hass, self.lock.entity_id)` | All 5 providers (2 as wrapper, 3 inline) | Add `@final` method to BaseLock |
| Raw `hass.services.async_call()` with manual error wrapping | Schlage, Akuvox | Use existing `self.async_call_service()` which already wraps errors |
| Optimistic `coordinator.push_update()` guard after set/clear | ZWaveJS, Matter (inconsistent guards) | Could standardize in base since it already knows about push vs poll |

### Should remove (unnecessary overrides/abstractions)

| Pattern | Issue | Proposed Change |
|---|---|---|
| `supports_code_slot_events = True` override | ZWaveJS, Matter override to return `True` — same as the default | Delete redundant overrides |
| `domain` as `@property` returning a constant | Every provider declares a 3-line property for a string constant | Make it a `ClassVar[str]` or a simple class attribute |

### Inconsistencies / hazards to fix

| Pattern | Issue |
|---|---|
| `coordinator.push_update` guard: Matter checks `coordinator.data is not None`, ZWaveJS doesn't | Pick one and standardize |
| `unsubscribe_push_updates` doesn't catch `ProviderNotImplementedError` | `subscribe_push_updates` catches it, asymmetric |
| `lock_config_entry = None` → always disconnected (undocumented) | VirtualLock has to override `async_is_integration_connected` to work around this |
| ZWaveJS uses `_listeners: list` AND `_value_update_unsub: Callable | None` | Two parallel subscription-tracking patterns in one class |

- `usercode_scan_interval` variations — legitimate per-provider differences
- `async_is_device_available()` check-via-fetch pattern — different calls needed per provider
- `async_hard_refresh_codes()` tag-then-get pattern — provider-specific tag step

| 9 | call_soon_threadsafe | **FIXED** — uses `hass.add_job` now |
| 10 | Connectivity vs availability conflated | **FIXED** — properly separated |

### Remaining / new issues:

**HIGH: Timeout and failures map to `SlotCode.EMPTY` (Issues 1, 7, 8)**

All three share the same root cause: communication failures in `async_get_usercodes` are indistinguishable from genuinely empty slots. A broad `except Exception` after the timeout also maps programming errors to EMPTY at debug level.

**Impact**: A temporary MQTT outage → all slots appear empty → sync manager attempts to reprogram every slot → storm of set operations on recovery.

**Fix**: Use `SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE` (or a new "unknown" sentinel) for timeouts/failures instead of EMPTY. Consider raising `LockDisconnected` when failures are systemic (most slots fail).

### Minor findings:

- Should use `self.get_managed_slots()` instead of importing from `..data` (project convention)
- `async_create_task` for coordinator refresh missing a descriptive name

## PR #1067 Combined Review — All 4 Agents

### Code Reviewer: **Clean, no issues**

### Silent Failure Hunter: **Clean** — one discussion point:
- `unsubscribe_push_updates` silently catches `ProviderNotImplementedError` while `subscribe_push_updates` re-raises it. Intentional asymmetry? If teardown is mandatory for push providers, this hides a contract violation. Could add a comment explaining why.

### Test Coverage: **No critical gaps** — two minor defensive paths untested (Z2M non-dict user_info, Z2M missing user field in pin_code), both criticality 4-5/10.

### Comment Analyzer: **Two actionable findings:**
1. **`async_is_integration_connected` docstring doesn't mention the raise** — callers expect a bool return. Should document that it raises `LockCodeManagerError` when `lock_config_entry` is None.
2. **BaseLock class docstring says "Do NOT raise bare `LockCodeManagerError`"** — but we now raise exactly that. Should qualify the prohibition to distinguish provider-side failures from internal programming errors.

Also noted: `managed_slots` property docstring could mention it aggregates across all config entries (not just the current one).

---

1	# Schlage Integration
2	
3	Lock Code Manager supports Schlage WiFi locks (Encode, Encode Plus) via the [Schlage](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/schlage/) integration.
4	
5	## How It Works
6	
7	Schlage locks manage codes by name. Lock Code Manager tags each code with `[LCM:<slot>]` in the name to track which codes it manages. For example, a code named "Guest" on slot 3 becomes `[LCM:3] Guest`.
8	
9	PINs are **write-only** — the Schlage cloud API returns masked codes (`****`). This means:
10	
11	- LCM can set and clear PINs on the lock
12	- The lock reports whether a code slot is occupied, but not the actual PIN value
13	- The code sensor shows the configured PIN (from LCM config) rather than the on-lock value
14	- On Home Assistant restart, LCM re-sets all configured PINs to guarantee correctness
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- The [Schlage](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/schlage/) integration configured in Home Assistant
19	- A Schlage WiFi lock (Encode, Encode Plus, or similar)
20	
21	## Supported Operations
22	
23	| Operation | Supported | Notes |
24	|-----------|-----------|-------|
25	| Set PIN | Yes | Via `schlage.add_code` service |
26	| Clear PIN | Yes | Via `schlage.delete_code` service |
27	| Read PIN | No | Schlage returns masked codes |
28	| Push updates | No | Polling every 5 minutes |
29	| Code slot events | No | Schlage does not report which code was used |
30	
31	## Limitations
32	
33	- **PINs are write-only**: LCM cannot verify the actual PIN on the lock.
34	- **No push updates**: Changes made via the Schlage app are not detected until the next poll (every 5 minutes).
35	- **No duplicate PINs**: Schlage locks reject setting the same PIN value on multiple codes. Each code must have a unique PIN.
36	- **Cloud-dependent**: All operations go through the Schlage cloud API.
37	
38	## Troubleshooting
39	
40	### Codes not appearing
41	
42	Ensure the Schlage integration is loaded and the lock entity appears in Home Assistant. LCM detects Schlage locks by their entity domain.
43	
44	### "Duplicate code name" errors
45	
46	LCM tags codes with `[LCM:<slot>]` prefixes. If you manually create a code with the same tagged name, LCM's set operation will fail. Remove the duplicate via the Schlage app.
47	
48	### "Duplicate PIN value" errors
49	
50	Schlage does not allow the same PIN on multiple codes. Ensure each LCM slot has a unique PIN.
51
